blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: Among knot invariants, the colored Jones polynomials $\{J_{K,n}\}_{n\geq2}$ and the Kashaev invariants $\{\langle K\rangle_N\}_{N\geq 2}$ are of particular interest, by their relation to quantum field theory, and the geometry of hyperbolic manifolds [@Witten1994; @MurakamiMurakami2001]. We refer to *e.g.* [@MurakamiMurakami2001; @Yokota2011] for their definitions; by [@MurakamiMurakami2001], the two invariants are related by $\langle K\rangle_N=J_{K,N}(\ifthenelse{\equal{}{}}{{\rm e}}{\operatorname{e}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(  \aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}{( )

blocks.title: Front matter
blocks.content:
MODULARITY AND VALUE DISTRIBUTION OF QUANTUM
INVARIANTS OF HYPERBOLIC KNOTS
S. BETTIN AND S. DRAPPEAU
Abstract. We obtain an exact modularity relation for the q-Pochhammer symbol. Using
this formula, we show that Zagier’s modularity conjecture for a knot K essentially reduces
to the arithmeticity conjecture for K. In particular, we show that Zagier’s conjecture holds
for hyperbolic knots K̸ = 72 with at most seven crossings. For K = 41, we also prove a
complementary reciprocity formula which allows us to prove a law of large numbers for the
values of the colored Jones polynomials at roots of u

blocks.title: Outline of the paper and sketch of the proofs
blocks.content: Theorem [\[th:1\]](#th:1){reference-type="ref" reference="th:1"} and Theorem [\[th:2\]](#th:2){reference-type="ref" reference="th:2"} are both based on two new relations for the $q$-Pochhammer symbol, given in Theorems [\[th:Ir\]](#th:Ir){reference-type="ref" reference="th:Ir"} (cf. [\[eq:mro\]](#eq:mro){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:mro"}) and [\[thp\]](#thp){reference-type="ref" reference="thp"}. These relations are proved in Section [\[repsec\]](#repsec){reference-type="ref" reference="repsec"} and both make use of the Abel-Plana summation formula [@Abel1992 p.23], [@Plana1820 p.408]

blocks.title: Notation
blocks.content:
Given $D\subset \mathbb{R}$ and $f:D\to\mathbb{R}$, we write $\|f\|_{\infty, D}:=\sup_{t\in D}|f(t)|$. Also, given $t\in\mathbb{R}$, we write $\|t\|:=\textnormal{dist}(t,\mathbb{Z})$ and $\{t\}:=t-\lfloor t\rfloor$, where $\lfloor t\rfloor$ is the integer part of $t$. Given a property $P$, we define ${\mathbf 1}_{P}$ (or ${\mathbf 1}(P)$) to be $1$ if the property $P$ is satisfied and $0$ otherwise.

All the implicit constants of the error terms are understood to be uniform in the various parameters unless otherwise indicated.
